answer: Divergent execution challenge licensing. At each epoch’s zenith, the registry draws a random seed. Each identity must return the output of a public deterministic kernel run with its private state. Clones cannot diverge, so duplicate outputs pile up like a dune of identical footprints; only the first claimant per output survives. An attacker pays a fresh per-identity salt, 1 MB storage, and 2^18 hash iterations per epoch to force divergence.
